title: Silver Below $60: Can It Fall Further?
speaker: Jeffrey Christian

macro_themes.view: Trade-weighted dollar moving sideways; central banks hold record dollar volumes; foreigners not dumping Treasuries.
Economic, political and post-election US problems should drive investors to buy more gold and silver over coming months into 2028.

calls.reason: Stuck in 4,050-4,200 range; the longer it stays low the greater chance of a spike to 4,000 or below; but expects investor buying to lift prices over months.
calls.quote: we do expect investors to step up their gold purchases and cause prices to rise. Um over the next several months and probably into 2028.

calls.reason: Weaker than gold, below $60, but doubts much further downside given October surprises and hostile post-election period.
calls.quote: We're not quite sure that we're going to see much further downside

calls.reason: Declining, but some reasons to think it could rise.
calls.quote: There are some reasons to think that the price could rise going forward, but just like gold and silver, platinum and palladium are showing weakness.

calls.reason: Dollar has moved sideways since H1 2025 and is not collapsing; safe-haven demand supports it.
calls.quote: the dollar is not collapsing... it has been basically moving sideways

notes: Gold 4,000 short-term is a risk scenario ("could spike down"), recorded as bearish target with that caveat. DXY 121 is the Fed trade-weighted index, not ICE DXY.
